basis: Wound infection produces botulinum toxin causing neuromuscular and autonomic blockade; respiratory weakness reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than lung damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy and cataracts define the disorder; feeding difficulties and unspecified gastrointestinal issues do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Classical complement deficiency is an immunodeficiency; associated infections and autoimmune diseases are separate diagnoses rather than universal organ damage.
Desmin-related muscular dystrophy with defining progressive cardiac conduction disease and later cardiomyopathy; skeletal muscle weakness may follow cardiac manifestations.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by shortening of the middle limb segments; no other organ involvement is established across the umbrella.
Cerebellar and caudate degeneration define disease; hearing loss in 2/2 assessed and ocular/skeletal findings in singletons do not establish prevalence across the 11-patient cohort.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; atrial septal defect, anemia and thrombocytopenia each occur in 30-79%. Dysmorphic features alone add no axes.
Hereditary prostate cancer affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; HOXB13 susceptibility does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Focal dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Parathyroid tumors cause hyperparathyroidism; osteoporosis/osteopenia and nephrocalcinosis are each annotated in 80-99%. Renal insufficiency itself is only occasional.
Diffuse poorly cohesive adenocarcinoma is predominantly gastric, supported by the representative example and sole child; this histologic umbrella does not specify another origin.
Benign smooth muscle tumor arising in the ureter; tumor location determines the axis rather than its smooth muscle histology.
Congenital dystroglycanopathy damages skeletal muscle; cerebellar atrophy and cerebral white matter abnormalities are annotated in 30-79%, despite preserved intellectual abilities.
Malignant glial tumor arising in the brain.
Familial thoracic aortic disease defined by aneurysm, dissection and rupture; no direct extra-vascular organ involvement is established.
Autoimmune inflammation of the supratentorial brain; characteristic neuronal antibodies support the immune mechanism.
Speech apraxia and language developmental impairment occur in 30-79%. Recurrent ear infections are separate diagnoses; structural ear defects and hearing loss are only occasional.
Congenital absence of eyelids and palpebral fissures with skin covering the globe; this is an ocular developmental defect.
Grade 2 oligodendroglioma is a primary central nervous system tumor; IDH mutation does not make the disease a systemic metabolic disorder.
ID, fifth-digit skeletal defects and ectodermal hallmarks define CSS4. Ptosis 9/12 and visual impairment 5/11 support ocular involvement; cap excludes hearing loss 4/12 and cleft palate 4/12.
Metastatic adrenal medullary tumor; direct metastases commonly occupy bone (~60-70%), liver (~40-50%) and lung (~30-50%). Neural ancestry does not establish CNS involvement.
Skeletal defects, microcephaly/intellectual impairment and cleft lip/palate are defining features; horseshoe kidney and urethral malformation are annotated in 30-79%.
ADAM10-related Alzheimer disease causes progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Borna virus infection directly causes encephalitis; no common extra-neural organ damage is established.
Sterol biosynthesis defect with defining microcephaly/developmental impairment and cataracts; psoriasiform dermatitis and ichthyosis occur in 1/1 annotated patients and are core features.
